A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and have readable text, equations, tables, and figures. v1 includes Appendix A.1–A.3; v2 ends after the references. Appendix omissions below refer specifically to the supplied v2.pdf.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark comparisons, architectural ablations, robustness experiments, and real-world tests, with additional qualitative results in Appendix A.3.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark comparisons, ablations, and robustness results, and reports successful detection in four real-world scenes.

M1.justification: The feature-volume construction, DINOv2 distillation, DBScan localization, RoI pooling, sparse attention, and two-stage training are retained. Separately naming the feature enhancement block reorganizes the description. Removing loss-weight symbols is equivalent to v1's implementation, where all three weights equal one.

E1.justification: ToysAD-8K and PartsAD-15K retain their task and dataset coverage. Real-world object coverage expands slightly: v2 Figure 7 adds Coca-Cola cans to the cups, medicine bottles, and bananas shown in v1 Figure 8.

E2.justification: Both versions evaluate the same COLMAP/DGCNN reconstruction-and-recognition pipeline, ImVoxelNet, and DETR3D. The Table 1 label changes from COLMAP to Recon-Recog, but the corresponding pipeline and comparator membership remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The real-world evaluation increases from three scenes to four, retaining five input views per scene. Benchmark splits, image and voxel resolutions, training budgets, AUC/accuracy metrics, IoU threshold, and quantitative robustness protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The quantitative ablations and view-count, object-count, and majority-ratio studies are retained. v2 extends the real-world case study and explicitly compares predictions with ground truth in failure cases (Figure 9). The PartsAD correspondence examples from v1 Figure 4 are absent from v2 Figure 6.

E5.justification: v1 Appendix A.2 states that standard deviation across multiple runs is below 0.5 for all experiments, including ablations. v2 has no corresponding variability or repeated-run statement. This establishes reduced reporting without establishing any change in runs performed.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 and Figure 5 retain their numerical results; for example, ToysAD-8K-Unseen remains 89.15 AUC and 81.57 accuracy. Qualitative evidence changes through the added successful can scene, revised examples and failure panels, and omission of many Appendix A.3 examples.

T1.justification: The task mapping, feature construction, reconstruction losses, correspondence operation, attention, and classification equations retain their mathematical substance. Correspondence indexing is clarified and unit loss weights are suppressed. Neither version introduces theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: Both versions claim a scene-relative, multi-view anomaly-detection task, two benchmarks, and an object-centric comparison method that generalizes to unseen objects and outperforms the retained baselines. Rewriting the abstract, introduction, and conclusion does not materially change these contributions.

C2.justification: The distillation explanation changes from producing identical features for matching geometries to producing very similar features. v1 Appendix A.1's discussion of readily adapting training to real manufacturing scenes through 2D supervision is omitted. Most interpretations of experimental trends and stated limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 retains core implementation settings and moves anomaly-quality checks into Section 4.1, but omits substantial appendix documentation: category assignments, DINOv2/KNN and Chamfer-based anomaly selection, rendering assets and software details, annotation guidance, GPU memory, and training times. The code/data release promise is retained.

R1.justification: Several cited works disappear, including Looking3D, Fishyscapes, Segment Me If You Can, and the Hendrycks–Gimpel baseline, alongside sources associated with omitted appendix material. The main positioning relative to anomaly detection, multi-view reconstruction, and feature distillation remains stable.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method, and experimental prose are extensively rewritten. The method overview is reorganized around four named components, feature enhancement receives its own subsection, and some appendix explanations enter the main text. The appendix and broader-impacts paragraph are omitted.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column layout and substantially redraws Figures 1–2. Qualitative examples use revised arrangements, multiple views, and yellow prediction boxes; analysis figures are relocated or reduced, and failure comparisons receive a separate figure. Table 3 and most appendix galleries are absent.

improvement.justification: v2 offers clearer diagrams, reorganized explanations, and more explicit failure illustrations, plus one additional real-world scene. However, it omits useful dataset-generation and split documentation and the sole repeated-run variability statement. With the core quantitative evidence unchanged, these losses make the supplied paper harder to reproduce and assess for repeatability, outweighing the presentation benefits.
